demos.title: The Scratchpad
details:
This tool was developed to address the need for pasting clean text from a Word document into a content management application. At my workplace, our content team frequently transfers content authored in Word into the CMT. Unfortunately, this process often introduces hidden characters and unwanted formatting from the Word document.

To mitigate these issues, I created this solution to reduce the likelihood of unwanted entities being pasted into the CMT. The tool automatically runs the text through several checks to ensure that no hidden entities or formatting errors are present before the text is entered into the CMT. This simple yet effective tool has significantly reduced the amount of post-entry work required to find, fix, and replace unwanted formatting and entities.

Styling
Bootstrap - for buttons and basic layout
Custom CSS - for everything else
Icons 8 @ https://icons8.com - for the bug, info, and lock icons

Scripting
Javascript - for logic and creating elements
JQuery - for functionality
RegEX - for some of the text validating functions

I decided to make my own modal and toggle switch for this, instead of using something from Bootstrap. Nothing super fancy, but it works. This one probably gets fiddled with the most since it is currently being used by people in my office. A bug will come up or a request made for something to be added. More requests than bugs 😉

demos.title: Trivia Quiz Challenge
details:
This is a simple multiple choice trivia quiz. It features 5-7 questions, each with four possible answers. Users can select their answers and submit the quiz to see their score.

It provides immediate feedback on the number of correct answers out of the total questions, allowing users to see how well they did.

This was the result of a challenge for a Javascript/Json API course I was taking. The goal was to create a quiz application that could dynamically load questions and answers from a JSON file, allowing for easy updates and modifications to the quiz content. I added a little css and other bits beyond what we did for the challenge because I thought it was a neat simple quiz that was worth sharing.

Styling
Custom CSS - 100%

Scripting
Custom Javascript - 100%
JSON Question Data - Open Trivia Database API
Local JSON File (backup) - for quiz questions and answers (questions generated by AI)

Instead of just using a local json file like in the challenge, I decided to add an actual API. The questions are generated from Open Trivia Database, very cool site. I have the local json file being used as a backup in case the API fails.

The Javascript/Json API course was a lot of fun. It was a great way to learn how to work with JSON data and create dynamic web applications. This quiz challenge was a perfect project to apply those skills. I enjoyed the process of designing the quiz, implementing the functionality, and testing it to ensure it worked smoothly. Overall, it was a rewarding experience that helped me improve my web development skills.

demos.title: ToDo List
details:
This page originally started as a simple to-do list project I created during an HTML class. Initially, it allowed users to add items to the list—nothing particularly special. However, one weekend, I decided to enhance its functionality.

The page now uses cookies for local storage (<-- Disabled in demo), enabling the list to be saved between sessions, due to not having access to a database at the moment.

Users can add items and mark them as completed. Once an item is completed, it moves to the "Done" area, where it can be undone by clicking on it and selecting "Undo". Please note that completed items are not permanently saved; the "Done" area resets once the browser is closed or refreshed, and the items can no longer be undone.

Additionally, the page supports the creation of sub-lists, allowing users to break down tasks into smaller steps or mini-tasks, which can also be marked as completed.

Styling
Bulma CSS - for basic layout and styling
Bootstrap Icons - for the icons being used
Custom CSS - for the personal touch

Scripting
Javascript - for creating elements and functionality

I didn't expect it, but I learned quite a bit while working on this project. I explored the Crypto interface, which I used to generate unique IDs for the list items, and also got a refresher on using cookies on the client side. Though I had worked with cookies before, it had been a long time, so revisiting this was a valuable experience.

What started as a way to pass the time turned into a surprisingly enjoyable project. Initially, I was just bored and looking for something to do, but enhancing the functionality of this to-do list has made it a tool I now use daily. Despite the abundance of to-do list apps available, I've grown fond of the simplicity of my own creation—though I might be a bit biased!
